title: Scaling analog values
summary: Scaling converts the raw integer of an analog module into an engineering value. It is a straight-line conversion defined by two points.

sections.heading: The straight line
sections.body:
```
value = (raw - rawMin) / (rawMax - rawMin) * (engMax - engMin) + engMin
```

For PLC Lab's generic profile (0..10000 for the nominal range) and a level of 0..100 %:

```
LevelPercent := INT_TO_REAL(LevelRaw) / 100.0;
```

sections.heading: Integer arithmetic traps
sections.body: In INT arithmetic `LevelRaw / 10000 * 100` is 0 for every value below 10000, because the division truncates first. Multiply first or convert to REAL before dividing. Also watch the INT range (-32768..32767): `LevelRaw * 100` overflows above 327.

sections.heading: Vendor helpers
sections.body: Most platforms provide scaling functions, for example NORM_X/SCALE_X on Siemens S7-1200/S7-1500 or module-level scaling to engineering units on Logix analog modules. The underlying mathematics is always the same straight line; check the exact raw range of your module.
